title: Cartesian monoidal straightening of a cocartesian fibration
statement:
Use the infinity categories, spaces and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], with a larger universe for categories of categories. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a cocartesian fibration of infinity categories: every arrow $f:b\to b'$ and $e\in\mathcal E_b$ admits a lift $e\to f_!e$ over $f$ such that, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the square of mapping spaces induced by this lift and by $p$ is a homotopy pullback. Write $\Phi:\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ for its classifying functor, with $\Phi(b)=\mathcal E_b$ and $\Phi(f)=f_!$. Products here are characterized by product mapping spaces and terminal objects by contractible mapping spaces into them. Assume $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal B$ have finite products, $p$ preserves them, and a product of $p$-cocartesian arrows is again $p$-cocartesian. Then $\Phi$ has a canonical lax symmetric monoidal structure for cartesian products. Its finite-arity structure functor is
$$\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal E_{b_i}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_{\prod_{i\in I}b_i},\qquad(e_i)\longmapsto\prod_{i\in I}e_i;$$
for $I=\varnothing$ this selects $1_{\mathcal E}\in\mathcal E_{1_{\mathcal B}}$. Here a symmetric monoidal infinity category means a cocartesian fibration over the nerve of finite pointed sets whose fiber over $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ is the $n$-fold power of its fiber over $\langle1\rangle$ via the inert projections, and lax symmetric monoidal means a functor over that nerve preserving cocartesian arrows above inert maps (those with singleton inverse images at every non-basepoint). Cartesian monoidal structures use finite products as their operations. Thus the asserted structure includes coherent compatibility with permutations, partitions into blocks, nullary operations and all higher simplices, not only binary comparison functors.

source.place: Ramzi, A monoidal Grothendieck construction for infinity-categories, Definition 1.11, Theorem 2.1 and Remark 2.2, specialized to cartesian monoidal structures.
